A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AAPT research and contain readable main text, Figures 1–8, Tables 1–6, and Appendices A–H. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, speed measurements, and ablations in Sections 3–4 and the appendices, including quantitative results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations, generated-video examples, speed measurements, and ablation findings from v1.

M1.justification: Section 2 and the appendices retain the same causal architecture, frame recycling, three-stage training procedure, adversarial objectives, and long-video training technique. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same VBench-I2V short- and long-video evaluations, pose-conditioned human generation, camera-conditioned world exploration, and five-minute extrapolation test. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4, including the I2V, pose-generation, camera-control, and speed comparisons. No baseline is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B, F, and G retain the same training schedules, resolutions, attention windows, evaluation metrics, sampling settings, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The training-duration ablation in Table 5, teacher-forcing comparison in Figure 7 and Appendix D, and result-recycling analysis in Appendix E are unchanged. No robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains five samples per prompt except one for SkyReel-V2. Neither version adds or revises seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, AAPT's 1440-frame temporal/frame quality remains 89.79/62.16 in Table 1, and single-H100 throughput remains 24.8 FPS in Table 4.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation and adversarial loss and regularization equations in Appendix B are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-step autoregressive generation, real-time performance, student-forcing training, and minute-long generation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of quality metrics and error accumulation are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning consistency, training cost, persistent artifacts, and five-minute extrapolation, together with the same appendix discussions.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures, camera preprocessing, and project-access information are unchanged. The added funding statement supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 125 reference entries are retained without substantive revision. Text flowing between pages 2 and 3 does not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 renames the acknowledgment to 'Acknowledgment and Disclosure of Funding' and adds that ByteDance Seed fully funded the work. It also adds a NeurIPS 2025 conference statement and updates the version/date markings; the scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The conference footer and spacing adjustments produce small layout shifts across pages 1–3. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds explicit funding transparency and conference formatting, but the scientific exposition, methods, evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations—including all appendices—remain unchanged. These limited administrative and layout edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
